lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach the project Azolla as a minute free-floating heterosporous fern with overlapping bilobed leaves, hanging roots and distinct micro- and megasporocarps, while explaining the older Azollaceae family treatment.

taxonomy_scope.historical_note: Flora of North America treats Azolla in Azollaceae. Current Kew synonymizes Azollaceae under Salviniaceae. The learner preserves Azollaceae as historical/search provenance only.

project_scope.note: The current project pool contains Azolla caroliniana. Kew accepts the species and includes Texas in its native range.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Pick up a tiny floating branch and use magnification. Look for overlapping two-lobed scale leaves in two rows, with a photosynthetic upper lobe and a thinner submerged lower lobe, plus roots hanging below.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Tiny free-floating aquatic ferns forming mats. Azolla has branched prostrate stems with alternate imbricate bilobed leaves and hanging roots.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Heterosporous. Sporocarps form near branch bases. Megasporocarps ultimately contain a single functional megaspore; microsporocarps contain many microsporangia whose microspores are grouped into massulae.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Tiny floating branched fern + overlapping bilobed leaves + hanging roots = Azolla/Salviniaceae. Species-level Azolla work often needs fertile material and microscopy.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: floating mat → single branch macro → upper/lower leaf lobes → hanging root → cyanobacterial cavity → micro- vs megasporocarp → old Azollaceae/current Salviniaceae card → microscopy caution
visual_lesson.intro: Azolla can look like green or reddish pond confetti. Under magnification it becomes unmistakably structured: a branched fern shoot with overlapping two-lobed leaves, roots, reproductive sporocarps and a built-in nitrogen-fixing symbiosis.

steps.title: 1 · Start with the floating mat
steps.look_for: Dense tiny green to reddish floating plants forming a mat rather than isolated duckweed-like fronds.
steps.why_it_matters: Establishes the growth form before magnification.

steps.title: 2 · Isolate one branch
steps.look_for: A branching prostrate axis covered by overlapping leaves arranged in two rows, with roots hanging below.
steps.why_it_matters: Shows that Azolla is a true branched fern shoot, not a pile of separate duckweed fronds.

steps.title: 3 · Split one leaf into two lobes
steps.look_for: An upper/emergent photosynthetic lobe and a thinner submerged lower lobe.
steps.why_it_matters: The bilobed leaf architecture is a core Azolla character.

steps.title: 4 · Show the cyanobacterial chamber
steps.look_for: A cavity in the dorsal/upper leaf lobe housing a nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterial symbiont.
steps.why_it_matters: Makes Azolla's famous nitrogen-fixing partnership understandable without implying the fern itself directly fixes nitrogen.

steps.title: 5 · Separate mega- and microsporocarps
steps.look_for: Megasporocarp with one functional megaspore versus microsporocarp with many microsporangia and grouped microspores/massulae.
steps.why_it_matters: Links Azolla to Marsileaceae through Salviniales heterospory while showing a very different sporocarp design.

steps.title: 6 · Learn the family-name change
steps.look_for: Older FNA/field-guide family: Azollaceae. Current Kew family: Salviniaceae.
steps.why_it_matters: Prevents two legitimate reference systems from looking like a database error.

steps.title: 7 · Know when species ID needs a microscope
steps.look_for: Sterile floating material lacks many of the megaspore, massula and leaf-hair characters used to distinguish Azolla species.
steps.why_it_matters: FNA notes that a large proportion of specimens lack sori and reliable species identification may require high magnification or SEM-level spore characters.

comparisons.title: Salviniaceae/Azolla vs Marsileaceae/Marsilea
comparisons.rule: Azolla is tiny and free-floating with overlapping bilobed scale leaves and hanging roots; Marsilea is rooted in mud with long petioles, four-part clover-like blades and hard sporocarps.

comparisons.title: Azolla vs duckweeds (Araceae)
comparisons.rule: Azolla has a branched stem with overlapping bilobed leaves, hanging roots and fern sporocarps. Duckweeds are reduced flowering plants built from discrete fronds and tiny flowers rather than a fern shoot.

comparisons.title: Azolla color caution
comparisons.rule: Green, reddish and crimson forms can all occur depending on condition and stress. Color is not a reliable family or species character.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not force Azolla to species from color or sterile mat appearance. Reliable species-level separation can depend on sporocarps, megaspore sculpturing, massulae and leaf-hair characters visible only under magnification.

genera.fast_cue: tiny free-floating branched mat + overlapping bilobed leaves + hanging roots + heterosporous sporocarps

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Accepted by current Kew; native range includes Texas.
Older FNA family placement retained as taxonomy/search provenance; current Kew includes Azolla within Salviniaceae.
